title: Bidual transpose identities for an exceptional pairing
statement:
Let $\mathcal T,\mathcal Z$ be monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category] with natural involutive symmetries $\sigma_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\cong Y\otimes X$ satisfying the hexagon identities. Suppose they are closed: for every $X$ there is an internal-Hom functor $[X,-]$ and bijections natural in all variables $\operatorname{Hom}(B,[X,H])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B\otimes X,H)$ with evaluation $[X,H]\otimes X\to H$ as counit. Fix objects $\omega_T\in\mathcal T$, $\omega_Z\in\mathcal Z$. Put $D_WX=[X,\omega_W]$ for $W=T,Z$, with the usual contravariant action, and define $\delta_X:X\to D_WD_WX$ as the transpose of $\mathrm{ev}_X\sigma_{X,D_WX}$.

Let $s,G:\mathcal T\to\mathcal Z$ be functors and let $h:G\omega_T\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_Z$. Fix strictly full subcategories $\mathcal S_T\subseteq\mathcal T$ and $\mathcal S_Z\subseteq\mathcal Z$ (objects closed under isomorphism, with all ambient morphisms between them). Assume $D_T,D_Z$ preserve their respective subcategories and $s,G$ send $\mathcal S_T$ into $\mathcal S_Z$. Let $q_{M,N}:sM\otimes GN\to G(M\otimes N)$ be given for $M,N\in\mathcal S_T$ and natural in both variables for morphisms of that full subcategory. No closure under internal Hom or tensor is assumed for these subcategories; those operations and the target of q are taken in the ambient categories. For every $K\in\mathcal S_T$ define
$$r_K=hG(\mathrm{ev}_K\sigma_{K,D_TK})q_{K,D_TK}\sigma_{GD_TK,sK},\qquad\alpha_K=\operatorname{transpose}(r_K):GD_TK\to D_ZsK.$$
For $L\in\mathcal S_T$ put $P=sD_TL$, $U=GL$, $c_L=\alpha_{D_TL}G\delta_L$, $b_L=hG(\mathrm{ev}_L)q_{D_TL,L}$ and $\beta_L=\operatorname{transpose}(b_L):P\to D_ZU$. Suppose for every $L\in\mathcal S_T$ the opposite-currying identity
$$\mathrm{ev}_P(c_L\otimes1_P)=b_L\sigma_{U,P}$$
holds. Then the following are identities of these specified morphisms:
$$\beta_L=D_Z(c_L)\delta_P,\qquad\beta_{D_TK}\,s(\delta_K)=D_Z(\alpha_K)\delta_{sK}.$$
The second equality has source $sK$ and target $D_ZGD_TK$. If $\alpha_{D_TL}$, $\delta_L$, and $\delta_P$ are isomorphisms, then $c_L$ and $\beta_L$ are isomorphisms. For the second identity, if $\alpha_K$ is invertible, equivalently $(D_Z\alpha_K)^{-1}\beta_{D_TK}\,s(\delta_K)=\delta_{sK}$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: inverse of the bidual composite is beta and evaluation identities give double-dual compatibility (old steps 6 and 9--10).

proof.text:
Use the tensor bifunctor and composition conventions of [def-sfb-monoidal-category]; all products below involve two factors only. In either ambient category, write $D=[-,\omega]$ and write $u_X:\operatorname{Hom}(B,DX)\to\operatorname{Hom}(B\otimes X,\omega)$ for uncurrying in the specified adjunction bijection. Naturality in $B$, applied to $a:B\to DX$ and $1_{DX}$, gives
$$u_X(a)=u_X(1_{DX})\circ(a\otimes1_X)=\mathrm{ev}_X\circ(a\otimes1_X).$$
The second equality is precisely the assumed counit normalization. As the inverse of a bijection, $u_X$ is injective. Thus it suffices to compare these evaluation composites when proving equality of maps into $DX$.

source.place: Counit formula and injectivity of the given adjunction bijection

proof.text:
The usual contravariant action $Df:DB\to DA$ for $f:A\to B$ is induced by precomposition in the internal-Hom variable. Naturality of the given bijection in that variable, applied to $1_{DB}$, says
$$\mathrm{ev}_A\circ(Df\otimes1_A)=\mathrm{ev}_B\circ(1_{DB}\otimes f).$$
Also, applying $u_{DX}$ to the defining transpose $\delta_X$ gives
$$\mathrm{ev}_{DX}\circ(\delta_X\otimes1_{DX})=\mathrm{ev}_X\circ\sigma_{X,DX}.$$
These are direct readings of the assumed natural bijections and the definition of $\delta$, with no invertibility assumption.

source.place: Naturality and the defining double-dual transpose

proof.text:
For the first identity fix $L$, and abbreviate $P=sD_TL$, $U=GL$, $c=c_L$, $b=b_L$, $D=D_Z$. Apply the preceding evaluation naturality to $f=c:U\to DP$, then the defining equation of $\delta_P$, and then naturality of $\sigma$:
$$\begin{aligned}
u_U(Dc\circ\delta_P)
&=\mathrm{ev}_{DP}\circ(\delta_P\otimes c)\\
&=\mathrm{ev}_P\circ\sigma_{P,DP}\circ(1_P\otimes c)\\
&=\mathrm{ev}_P\circ(c\otimes1_P)\circ\sigma_{P,U}.
\end{aligned}$$
The opposite-currying hypothesis makes the last expression $b\circ\sigma_{U,P}\circ\sigma_{P,U}=b$. Since $u_U(\beta_L)=b$ by definition and $u_U$ is injective, this proves $\beta_L=D_Z(c_L)\circ\delta_P$.

source.place: Second paragraph: identify beta with the dual of c followed by delta

proof.text: Under the three stated isomorphism hypotheses, $G(\delta_L)$ has inverse $G(\delta_L^{-1})$, by the functor identity and composition axioms. Hence $c_L=\alpha_{D_TL}\circ G(\delta_L)$ has inverse $G(\delta_L^{-1})\circ\alpha_{D_TL}^{-1}$. Contravariant functoriality makes $D_Z(c_L^{-1})$ the inverse of $D_Z(c_L)$. The first identity therefore gives the two-sided inverse $\delta_P^{-1}\circ D_Z(c_L^{-1})$ for $\beta_L$. This verifies both asserted isomorphisms using only their listed factors.

source.place: First displayed bidual composite and its canonical inverse

proof.text:
For the second identity fix $K\in\mathcal S_T$ and put $A=sK$, $Q=GD_TK$, $D=D_Z$. Duality stability gives $D_TK,D_TD_TK\in\mathcal S_T$. Since this subcategory is full, $\delta_K:K\to D_TD_TK$ is a morphism to which first-variable naturality of $q$ applies. It gives
$$q_{D_TD_TK,D_TK}\circ(s\delta_K\otimes1_Q)=G(\delta_K\otimes1_{D_TK})\circ q_{K,D_TK}.$$
Here the tensor objects and the target of $q$ remain ambient; no closure of $\mathcal S_T$ under tensor or internal Hom has been used.

source.place: Second paragraph: first-variable naturality of the exceptional tensor comparison

proof.text:
Uncurry the left side of the desired second identity using the counit formula and the definition of $\beta_{D_TK}$, then substitute step 5 and the defining transpose equation for $\delta_K$ from step 2:
$$\begin{aligned}
u_Q(\beta_{D_TK}\circ s\delta_K)
&=b_{D_TK}\circ(s\delta_K\otimes1_Q)\\
&=h\circ G\bigl(\mathrm{ev}_{D_TK}\circ(\delta_K\otimes1_{D_TK})\bigr)\circ q_{K,D_TK}\\
&=h\circ G(\mathrm{ev}_K\circ\sigma_{K,D_TK})\circ q_{K,D_TK}.
\end{aligned}$$
Every line is a map $A\otimes Q\to\omega_Z$; the middle line also uses preservation of composition by $G$.

source.place: Second paragraph: uncurrying beta of the dual after s(delta)

proof.text:
Uncurry the right side by evaluation naturality for $\alpha_K:Q\to DA$, the definition of $\delta_A$, and naturality of symmetry:
$$\begin{aligned}
u_Q(D\alpha_K\circ\delta_A)
&=\mathrm{ev}_{DA}\circ(\delta_A\otimes\alpha_K)\\
&=\mathrm{ev}_A\circ\sigma_{A,DA}\circ(1_A\otimes\alpha_K)\\
&=\mathrm{ev}_A\circ(\alpha_K\otimes1_A)\circ\sigma_{A,Q}\\
&=r_K\circ\sigma_{A,Q}.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is the defining transpose equation of $\alpha_K$. Expanding $r_K$ cancels $\sigma_{Q,A}\circ\sigma_{A,Q}=1_{A\otimes Q}$, so the result is exactly the last expression of step 6. Injectivity of $u_Q$ proves $\beta_{D_TK}\circ s\delta_K=D_Z(\alpha_K)\circ\delta_{sK}$.

source.place: Second paragraph: compare the other transpose and cancel the two symmetries

proof.text: If $\alpha_K$ is invertible, the inverse of $D_Z(\alpha_K)$ is $D_Z(\alpha_K^{-1})$, by contravariant functoriality. Composing the second identity on the left with this inverse gives $(D_Z\alpha_K)^{-1}\circ\beta_{D_TK}\circ s(\delta_K)=\delta_{sK}$. Conversely, composing that equation on the left with $D_Z\alpha_K$ recovers the second identity, by cancellation. This establishes the final equivalent form with source $sK$ and target $D_ZD_ZsK$.
